key_insight: The paper shows that optimal stock orders under censored demand can be learned directly from covariates by minimizing a new model-agnostic loss function, avoiding explicit demand reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a scalable way to build data-driven inventory policies from real retail logs, with implementations compatible with linear models, kernel methods, and deep networks.
method: Defines a custom loss whose minimizer matches the optimal newsvendor policy under censored observations.
Uses a single estimation step on observational data with known past stocking quantities.
Provides excess-risk generalization bounds for linear, kernel, and neural network implementations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports fast convergence on synthetic data and improved performance on real-world retail data, with scalability to hundreds of thousands of samples.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of observed covariates and censored-demand data, and practical results may vary if the censoring mechanism or past-order information is noisy.
paper_title: Optimal Feature-Based Newsvendor Policies under Censored Demand
